steps.body: Adding two numbers with the **same sign** is straightforward: add their sizes (magnitudes) and keep the shared sign. -3 + (-5): both negative, so add 3+5=8, keep negative: -8.

widget.successFeedback: −7. Two debts do not cancel each other — they add. Same signs pile up, and the sign of the pile is the sign you started with.
widget.lowFeedback: Your pile is worth less than −7 (too far negative).
widget.highFeedback: Your pile is worth more than −7. Both numbers are negative, so no positive chips belong here.

predict.prompt: Building −3 + (−4) with chips: will any chips cancel?

options.label: No — every chip points the same way

predict.reveal: Cancelling needs OPPOSITE chips, and here every chip is negative — seven − chips simply stack up to −7. Same signs pile; only different signs fight.

cml.actionGoal: Add and remove zero pairs while tracking the net signed value.

explanation.prompt: Why does a positive chip paired with a negative chip preserve value?

options.label: Their values sum to zero.
options.feedback: Exactly. A zero pair changes the model but not the net value.

options.label: Two chips always increase the value by two.
options.feedback: That describes a surface feature, not the mathematical relationship that must remain true. A zero pair changes the model but not the net value.

steps.body: Picture it on the number line: -3 + (-5) means starting at -3 and jumping 5 MORE to the left, landing at -8 — both jumps go the same direction.

commonErrors.feedback: Both numbers are negative, so the sum stays negative: -7 + (-9) = -16.
That subtracts instead of adding magnitudes. Add 7+9=16, keep the sign: -16.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add the magnitudes 7+9=16, keep the shared negative sign: -16.
